_doc: How tools/audio.py drives Dragon Slayer's sound engine. RAM names come from ram.inc. PlaySong / PlaySfx take the number in A. The game runs the engine from its LCD interrupt (LCDStatHandler.sound: UpdateSoundRegisters, then TickSound, then the handler's pops and reti); 'update' enters there, with the return address for that reti placed above the stack by 'setup'. Six channels: 4 music (square 1, square 2, wave, noise), 2 effect (square 1, noise); a song or effect counts as playing while one of its channel states is not 0.

loop_frames._doc: [update where the loop starts, update where it jumps back]: every part of these songs ends with $FE (start over) and all parts have the same length, so the song repeats after length x 8 / tempo updates; the first notes sound at update 1

music 1: PlayFieldMusic: on the map (numbers $00-$05, $07, $09, $0A, $0D and $0E play this song too)
music 6: PlayFieldMusic once the dragon has been beaten three times; first after its third defeat
music 11: StartGame / ContinueGame: the PHASE n / START ! screen
music 12: PhaseClear: twice on the phase-clear screen
music 17: EnterWarp: the hero appears at the other end
sfx 5: A find or gold; the dragon flashes
sfx 10: The hero's blow does no damage
sfx 12: TurnEnd: no damage, or a potion stolen
